A drowned abyss of deep green-black water inside architecture far too large to be a building: on the right two thirds, colossal stone piers and a single immense round-topped arch rise out of still black water and vanish upward into darkness; the arch and its perfect reflection in the water together form one tall almond shape with a dim cold light at its centre, suggesting a vast eye without drawing one. Every file was inspected at full size and at phone size; the papers and photographs carry no writing, the eye is concentric rings in stonework, and both corner pieces read the same across the diagonal. Second pass, also 2026-11-21: the first set read as a pleasant ruin and a cosy desk, so the night frame, both corners and both backdrops were repainted (v2) to unsettle: limbs wound around mismatched stone rails, a ring-and-slit eye mark shared by the stone boss and the wax seal, a drowned abyss of wrong scale, and an evidence wall whose strings meet on a torn-out photograph. The first versions are listed under retired with their prompts. Limbs appear as limbs only: no head, face or body, and no named being from any published work. The two textures and the day frame are unchanged. Third pass, also 2026-11-21: the limbs on the night frame and corner were cords at screen size, so both were repainted (v3) with two heavy limbs twisted around every rail and knotted over the eye, toothed suckers and cracked stone. Still limbs only: no head, face or body.
